summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant status, and recent loss of her father was admitted for leg swelling and malaise following a urinary tract infection. She had gained 7 pounds despite self-administering old Lasix tablets. Evaluation showed no acute cardiopulmonary process, no DVT, and stable kidney function. Her white count initially rose but improved, and blood cultures were negative. CMV was not detected, and EBV testing indicated past but not active infection. She was continued on cefpodoxime for the UTI and started on a scheduled regimen of furosemide every other day. Her symptoms improved during the admission, and she was discharged home with instructions to monitor weight, continue antibiotics, and follow up with her transplant team and weekly labs.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Age-related osteoporosis without current pathological fracture
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of breast
